newsitem.title: UK: Camelot lottery payout delayed by hitch.
newsitem.headline: Camelot lottery payout delayed by hitch.

text.p: Camelot, operator of the British national lottery, faced embarrassment on Sunday after it was forced to freeze pay-outs from its Saturday night draw.
A Camelot spokeswoman told Reuters that the jackpot had been won but that "because of a technical hitch we are still unable to issue confirmed results."
"At the moment we are unable to pay out any prizes to players," she said. The company was working to sort out the problem but it could take "up to a couple of days".
Until the announcement is made, not even the lowest prize of 10 pounds ($16.40) can be claimed.
It was the second time Camelot has been unable to give the number of winners on the same evening as the draw.
In November computer terminals across Britain crashed during the afternoon and the whole system had to be re-started.
This time it was a problem with processing the information, which did not tally when checked, the spokeswoman said, adding there was "no question whatsoever of fraud."

Oflot, the lottery regulator, said there should be a report into what went wrong. A spokeswoman said: "We are watching developments closely and will be calling for a full incident report once the problem has been resolved."
